newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $1.50 lower, Brent down 5-10 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $1.50 lower, Brent down 5-10 cts.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to open lower as they caught up with overnight falls, with Brent also seen a touch lower at the open.

July gas oil was expected to open around $1.50 lower from its previous closing price of $163.75 a tonne. August Brent was seen five to 10 cents down at the open from $18.08 a barrel at the prior close.
Dealers said the falls would come as both markets caught up with overnight falls on the U.S. and Singapore markets which came after bearish data from the American Petroleum Institute.
July heating oil was last bid 0.40 cent lower at 52.05 cents a gallon by 0800 GMT in overnight ACCESS trading.
Figures from the API showed U.S. crude imports hit a record 9.4 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ended June 13, up nearly a million bpd on the previous week.

Total crude stocks fell 880,000 barrels to 323.1 million but were still 16.4 million above a year ago. The decline included a fall of 2.6 million on the more volatile West Coast, which tends to be discounted.

At the same time, gasoline output set a record 8.23 million bpd after breaking the record set two weeks prior. Its inventories rose 1.7 million barrels to 204.1 million, cutting its deficity to a year ago to 1.2 million.
Distillate supplies jumped 3.3 million and were 13.2 million above a year ago.
"The API figures were a bit bearish so I think we'll just drift down in line with the overnight falls," one dealer said.
